record_notes.DCP-LETT-1863: May 2, supplied 1856, fourteen blocks and complete notes/bibliography read. Explicit April 8 Gray note missing; no direct prompt recovered. Proposes geographic comparisons excluding Arctic/alpine and cultivated aliens, emphasizes genus relationships beyond shared species. P2 100/500 and two 200/500 classes are hypothetical illustration, not measured flora. Questions family versus genus size/range, sociality of naturalized plants, variability versus marked races, growth at limits and Fuegian connections. Protean genera comparison requested, numbered species list suggested. P12 endorses six essay heads but their full source missing. Published Gray adoption and Darwin May 1 calculation in apparatus are separate evidence; future article not current letter text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1926: July 14, supplied 1856, four blocks and complete notes/bibliography read. Has read Gray North Carolina paper; asks if Alleghenies permit migration, admits not knowing Oconee location. Requests progress on distribution essay and northern limits; asks whether intermediate varieties less numerous, recalls May 2 naturalized-plant query. These are questions rather than established corridors or ratios. Later cancelled citation and replacement Gray statistics are future layers. 1934 P5–7 explicitly answers intermediate-variety query; mountain answer may lie in missing beginning and is not restored.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1934: Incomplete Gray letter assigned early August 1856 from approximate transatlantic interval; twelve blocks, annotations, all notes/bibliography read. Opening mid-sentence describes school Manual, four statistical pages and enclosed last proof page, not full book. Last proofs revised today, publication later August, holiday and meeting planned. Invites Darwin travel and acknowledges photo. P5–7 tentative intermediate-rarity impression with strong nomenclatural/sample-selection caveats: named type can be rare and intermediates abundant; Mentha example qualified. P8 no actual study of introduced variability yet, offhand guess not confirmation. Asks early critique of essay sheets, offers correspondence. Explicit Darwin docket Received Aug20 /1856/ supplies arrival distinct from inferred early-August composition; other pencil/crayon notes undated. Supports 1944 P1–2/P6; missing earlier pages/proof page not reconstructed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1944: August 24, supplied 1856, six blocks and full notes/bibliography read. Explicitly values Gray indefinite answers, qualifies Wollaston intermediate-rarity claim, reports Watson agreement on agrarian variability. Declines US visit for health, wants essay sheets not already full receipt. P3 Watson 1835 table 499 shared/110 non-Arctic, and Watson/Syme current 20–25 examples; six named taxa match 1891 appended list, Syme count matches 1907. These are separate inputs from Gray. P4 321 shared count derives enclosed Manual proof, not all in surviving 1934 body. P6 asks continued naturalized variability observation. Direct Gray scope P1–2/P6, Watson knowledge separately recorded. August20 receipt docket earlier than August24 response.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1959: Gray September 23, 1856, seventeen blocks, annotations, all notes/bibliography read. Engelmann is George per authority note, not Theodor as editorial summary says. P1 introduced variability opinion tentative. Specific social Barberry, Maruta, Hypericum, Verbascum examples attributed partly to Engelmann/Agassiz, German comparison limited; dispersal/climate explanations hypotheses. Erodium introduced status and Spanish abundance qualified. Indigenous weed increase and range spread not equally proven. Duplicate first essay sent after possible failed Trubner forwarding; later receipt must be checked. Future tabulations and details proposed, omitted Cassiope/Loiseleuria supplied as correction. Three-fourths northward expectation explicitly not counted; Convallaria counterexample and Guyot 6700ft barometric report, no true alpine flowering species known there. Repeats invitation. Responds May2 social questions and August24 range/invitation discussion. Received October11 per 1973.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1973: October 12, supplied 1856, eleven blocks, complete notes/bibliography and quarter MathML read. Letter September 23 and one Statistics copy received yesterday October 11; another copy two days previously (relative to latter receipt), not evidence letter arrived with first copy. Praises first article and approves detail, thanks social/variable facts and approximate quarter of shared European plants not extreme-northern: 1/4 is genuine MathML, not14. Further requests introduced genera/orders, Asia climate explanation and excluding mundane genera; no answered statistics yet. Corrects AND to NOT table-header misprint and reprint pagination, important original error but underlying complete article not admitted here. P6–7 acknowledge planned range calculations. Hooker visit future and review query new. Direct surviving-letter response P1–2/P6–7, detailed paper-specific critique separate pending full paper context.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1999: November 24, supplied 1856, seven blocks and all notes/bibliography read. Explicit November 4 letter thanks for northern facts, enclosures forwarded on same receipt day without independently naming day. Earlier November 18 Hooker witness retained. Book ordered months ago, still hoped soon, not possessed/read. P4 first troubled by Arctic-continent phrase then notices Labrador/Greenland qualifier and revises interpretation within same paragraph; retain sequence, not initial misreading alone. P5 answers show-the-way self-deprecation. P7 repeats surprise at earlier variability opinion, explicitly distinguishes marked races; not a newly quantified November 4 claim. Direct scope P1–5, separate closing/older-topic continuation retained as grounding.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2034: January 1, supplied 1857, seven blocks and full notes/bibliography read. Second Statistics part received/read, substantial data response relies on paper not a surviving current cover letter. Supports large-genus range relation but dislikes Greenland alpine route; Agassiz Nature-never-lies anecdote from Lyell is irony about theorists, not endorsed infallibility. Proposes comparing 320 shared species,115 representatives + 15 marked varieties=130 and additional categories; not already completed study. P4 reports own British and Hooker NZ three-class tree/sex comparisons, matching 2014; theoretical explanation still conditional, Tasmania analysis future. P7 asks US protean genera and wrongly supposes no Rosa; laterGray correction not backdated. Missing present cover/input not manufactured. Existing December 10 Hooker knowledge retained when adding January 1 cross-correspondent witness.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1891: Additional Watson June 5, 1856, nine retained blocks including complete long six-taxon appended list, annotations, all notes and bibliography read. Recasts missing Darwin letter as four questions. Supports earlier publication but no publication completed. Describes three forms of geography work and unpublished 39-species fragment; old table incomplete/outdated. Northern absence exceptions hinge identity/nativity. Agrarian 40–50 strict and similar broader group, no greater average variability, two strong Polygonum/Viola exceptions and annual/perennial hypothesis. Full list Chrysosplenium/Isnardia/Astragalus/Thlaspi/Arenaria/Lythrum has cautious taxonomy, introductions and range qualifications; exact six reused in 1944 P3. Do not upgrade doubtful species identity or force categorical zero exceptions. Darwin notes undated; laterreplacement by Gray apparatus not contemporary. Available by August 24 witness, possible earlier Watson response pending packet 20.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1907: Additional Watson June 20, 1856, twelve blocks, annotations, all notes/bibliography read. Old 1835 table now dated and corrections needed. Quotes Syme views in P3–4, separately attributed; 22 candidate species from Gray Manual, 5–6 possible introductions plus islands/aquatic/littoral qualifications. Asian-American comparison data insufficient, no definitive route via Kamchatka. Hypothetical Spain/Ireland connections and climate tolerance, glacier suitability doubted. Darwin 1944 P3 explicitly cites Syme assistance and 20–25 qualified species, establishing knowledge by August 24, not exact arrival. Later Asa Gray disagreement in manuscript apparatus not backdated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1695: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. June 8, supplied 1855. Explicitly answers Gray May 22, suggests geographic range codes and comparisons, explains exploratory rather than fixed questions, seeks close-species marks and queries inconsistent mountain distances. P3 compares family proportions then admits apparent agreement fails across other families. Crucially the preserved raw HTML itself contains flattened numerals 361798=149, 1092=19.2, 24206=18 and 2231798=18, with no MathML nodes: do not describe this as merely an extractor bug or silently reconstruct fractions/arithmetic. Hold reliable rendering of those numerical passages pending authoritative source verification. Later Gray publication is future; full scientific letter is an established response, with rendering hold.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1707: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Explicit prior primary reading reused from accepted batch-05 with source and note/ledger pins. Additional full reading of Gray June 30, 1855, explicitly answering June 8. Promises annotated Manual sheets with close species, discusses taxonomy and burden of evidence, plans newspaper reprinting and Morris fish-egg enquiry. Distinguish proposed sheets from later manuscript delivery and planned enquiry from already dispatched Morris June 17 letter described by editors. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1725: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. July 21, supplied 1855. Explicitly thanks for June 30 letter, close-species discussion and intended marking, while not knowing whether sheets arrived and suspecting they did not. Hooker has now read the Gray letter, unlike the earlier May letter merely forwarded. Hopes Gray writes species essay and distribution account; they are not complete. Postscript reports listed seeds germinated after eighty-two/eighty-five days, answering Gray interest. Entire four-block reply supported by 1707; physical marked-sheet receipt is not established.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1749: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. August 24, supplied 1855. Responds to a different missing Gray letter received about a fortnight earlier, with note forwarded to Hooker and manuscript close-species list. This is not June 30 promised marked sheets. Gives 115 genera and 6.37 versus 4.67 species per genus, with Salix/Carex and single-species genera exclusions; claims qualified support and asks for possible fallacy. Separate enquiry about variable organs cites Helianthemum and Pyrgoma; preserve report/example qualifications. Missing Dytiscus update and full manuscript list prevent direct training pair with 1707.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1982: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Additional Gray November 4, 1856 source, all twenty-five blocks including initial eight statistical rows, notes, annotations and bibliography read. Rough 320 European-shared species, 230 not detected inside Arctic circle, minus about twelve alpine/subalpine gives 218; nested latitude thresholds are 155/113/56/20/5, not disjoint bins. Only one of final five a reliable case. Apparatus mentions earlier 321; preserve versions. Answers October 12 letter, later research may extend ranges. Introduced orders supplied while genera requested; list copying not done, reference to buy book not receipt. East Asia climate relation not full causal explanation. Work on mundane genera and corrected lists future. Criticises Hooker conifer ranking; asks Darwin post enclosures. Raw diag/ramme table layout held; Darwin notes undated. Distinctive range facts and conifer rap identify forwarding/knowledge in 1991 by November 18.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2014: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December 7, 1856 Hooker ALS, fifteen retained blocks, all notes/annotations/bibliography. Rough NZ counts and uncertain mono/dioecious categories deliberately qualified. Body says 756 species, 108 trees, 150 shrubs; table rows total 757 and 149 shrubs, as Darwin separately totals. Do not silently reconcile. Table: herbs 379/102/19, shrubs 88/30/31, trees 56/40/12; 102 includes 55 Compositae. 234 separated/incomplete flowers matches column combination, taxonomic and developmental caveats remain. Raw diag/ramme and flattened rows require rendering care. Tasmania review promised in months. P11 private Lyell review-authorship anecdote and P13 Emma inquiry separately answered in 2018. P14–15 additional Clematis/Viola/Compositae/grass qualifications, separate undated Darwin calculations not Hooker original conclusions.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
